subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: For Darwin gateway exec, should allowlisted shell-shaped commands with tilde or other shell expansion become auto-executable after safe normalization, or should those command shapes remain explicit-approval-only with clearer docs and warnings?
rationale: The broad docs wording supports the reporter's expectation, but the current code intentionally fails closed when OpenClaw cannot materialize an enforced command plan.

options.title: Normalize Safe Shell Shapes
options.body: Handle narrow cases such as tilde expansion or independently allowlisted simple chains without bypassing enforcement, then add Darwin/source regression coverage.

options.title: Document Prompt-Only Shapes
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed behavior and update docs plus warning text to explain that shell expansion and other unenforceable shapes require explicit approval on Darwin.

options.title: Allow Raw Matched Shell Text
options.body: Run any allowlist-matched Darwin shell command without an enforced plan, accepting a larger security-boundary change.

recommendation.title: Normalize Safe Shell Shapes
recommendation.body: Handle narrow cases such as tilde expansion or independently allowlisted simple chains without bypassing enforcement, then add Darwin/source regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history trail for gateway exec approval behavior points to @vincentkoc's remote approval regression work.
